ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The left side of the figure is an ideal transformer circuit. On the left side of the primary coil there are two input terminals c and d; above the primary coil there is point a, and in the middle there is tap b. Switch S can connect to a or b; the right side of the secondary coil is connected to load resistor R, and ideal meters are connected. The right side of the figure gives the graph of the sinusoidal AC voltage u applied to the primary-side c and d terminals as a function of time t. The horizontal axis is labeled t/×10^-2 s. Two adjacent in-phase positions of the waveform are separated by 2 horizontal-axis units, so the period T = 2×10^-2 s. Then reason: From the graph, read T = 0.02 s, so the frequency f = 1/T = 50 Hz. An ideal transformer only changes the amplitudes of voltage and current; switch S connected to a or to b only changes the effective number of turns on the primary side and the transformation ratio, and does not change the frequency of the alternating current. Therefore the current frequency in resistor R is always 50 Hz. The direction of a sinusoidal alternating current changes 2 times in each period, so the number of direction changes in 1 s is 2f = 2×50 = 100 times.
